skill.displayName: Local Markdown Editor with Live Preview 本地Markdown网页编辑器

version.changelog:
Initial release of xi-markdown: a local, web-based Markdown editor with live preview and advanced features.

- Real-time editing and synchronized preview using a local Flask server.
- Comprehensive toolbar for all markdown elements, with responsive dark and light themes.
- Easily open, edit, and save markdown files—supports file selection, relative paths, and direct URL opening.
- Auto server shutdown when the editor page is closed; manual shutdown also available.
- Includes useful keyboard shortcuts for productivity.
- RESTful API for file operations and markdown preview.

llm.summary: The skill is mostly what it claims (a local Flask-based markdown editor) but contains several implementation choices that increase the risk of accidental data exposure or remote access (unsanitized URL-to-JS injection, wide CORS, and unrestricted file read/write).

dimensions.detail: The name/description (local markdown editor with live preview and file save) aligns with the code and SKILL.md: the app reads, renders, and saves files and exposes preview endpoints. Those file I/O capabilities are expected for an editor, but some implementation details (ability to read/write arbitrary absolute filesystem paths and URL parameter file loading) increase attack surface relative to the stated 'local' usage.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs running the Flask server and explicitly supports opening arbitrary files via the ?file=path URL parameter and relative/absolute paths. The server code injects the raw file parameter directly into index.html JavaScript (no escaping) and exposes endpoints that return file contents and allow saving arbitrary paths — these extend beyond simple rendering into broad filesystem access and include an unsafe string injection point.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec — instruction-only plus included Python script. Dependencies are standard Python packages for this use-case (flask, flask-cors, markdown) and are declared in documentation. No external code download or archive extraction is used by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials, which is proportionate for a local editor. The file I/O and server behavior are intrinsic to the stated functionality; however, because it can read/write arbitrary filesystem paths, it effectively requires trust that the server will remain local and not exposed to other hosts.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-on and does not request platform-level privileges. It starts a local Flask server and can be invoked by the user. This is consistent with its purpose; the risk comes from the server's access to arbitrary files and its exposure surface (CORS, possible host binding).
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This package appears to be a legitimate local markdown editor, but install and run only after you accept the following risks and take mitigations: 

- Arbitrary file read/write: The server exposes endpoints that can read and overwrite files given a path (including absolute paths). Only run it on machines where you trust the environment and avoid running as an elevated user. Prefer opening specific files (not root or system dirs).

- Unsanitized URL injection / XSS risk: The app injects the ?file parameter directly into the served HTML/JavaScript without escaping, which could allow crafted input to execute in the browser. Do not expose the server to untrusted networks or embed it in pages you don't control.

- Network exposure & CORS: The app enables CORS for all routes. If the Flask server is bound to 0.0.0.0 (check the bottom of app.py when launching), remote websites could call its APIs and access files. Ensure the server binds to 127.0.0.1 or a specific local interface, or remove/limit CORS if you modify the code.

- External resources: index.html loads libraries (marked, DOMPurify, Font Awesome) from CDNs. If you need an air-gapped or more secure setup, vendor those libraries locally.

Recommended steps before running:
- Inspect the bottom of scripts/app.py to confirm it binds only to localhost and does not disable host restrictions.
- If you will use this, modify the code: 1) escape/URL-decode and safely JSON-encode any inserted file path before embedding in HTML, 2) restrict file access to a workspace directory (deny absolute paths outside workspace), 3) limit or remove CORS, and 4) avoid running as admin/root.

If you cannot inspect or modify the code, treat this skill as potentially exposing sensitive local files and avoid running it on systems with secrets or on machines reachable from untrusted networks.
